steps.message:
I stopped before editing. `client.py` is shared, and the change wouldn't stay in staging.

`scripts/export_prod.py:5` points the same client at `https://reports.example.com` (production), and `scripts/sync_staging.py:5` points it at staging. Both import `fetch_report`/`list_reports` from `client.py`. Putting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls (`client.py:11`, `client.py:17`) disables certificate validation for the nightly production export as well — that traffic becomes interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection, and it fails silently rather than erroring. `urllib3` will also start emitting `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.

The self-signed staging cert is a real problem worth solving; the blanket flag just solves it in the one place that also covers production.

questions.question: How should the self-signed staging cert be handled, given client.py is shared with the production export?

options.label: Env-driven verify (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS / REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env knob read in client.py, passed as requests' verify=. sync_staging.py opts out (or points at the staging CA); export_prod.py keeps full verification by default.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere and point it at the staging cert file. Strictest option, but needs the cert available on disk wherever sync_staging.py runs.

options.label: Blanket verify=False
options.description: What you asked for: both calls in client.py get verify=False. Production nightly export loses cert validation too. I'll do this if you confirm.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py:10-24` — `_tls_verify()` resolves `requests`' `verify`: a `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` path if set, else `False` when `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` is falsey, else `True`. Both `requests.get` calls now pass it.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:6-8` — defaults `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`, so the staging sync skips verification as you wanted.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; sets neither variable, so the nightly production export still verifies certs.

Two notes:

- `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on each staging call. I left it in place rather than suppressing it — it's an accurate signal, and silencing it would also hide an accidental opt-out elsewhere. Say the word if you want it quieted.
- If you can get the staging CA onto the box that runs the sync, `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging-ca.pem` restores verification there with no code change.

Checks: `ruff check` is clean on `client.py`; the two `RUF100` hits are pre-existing `# noqa: E402` directives in both scripts (no project ruff config enables E402) — I left them alone. `mypy` reports only missing `types-requests` stubs, an environment gap, not a code error. No tests exist in this repo. Nothing committed.
